name: Nelson Mandela
info: Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela (1918–2013) was a South African anti-apartheid revolutionary who spent 27 years in prison, negotiated the end of apartheid and served from 1994 to 1999 as the country's first black president.

facts.born: 18 July 1918, in the village of Mvezo in Umtata, then part of South Africa's Cape Province; a Xhosa of a cadet branch of the Thembu royal family, son of the chief Gadla Henry Mphakanyiswa Mandela and Nosekeni Fanny
facts.died: 5 December 2013, aged 95, at his home in Houghton, Johannesburg, after a prolonged respiratory infection; state funeral on 15 December in Qunu
facts.role: Lawyer; national president of the ANC Youth League (from 1950); co-founder and chairman of Umkhonto we Sizwe (1961); President of the African National Congress (1991–1997); President of South Africa (1994–1999); Secretary-General of the Non-Aligned Movement (1998–1999)
facts.known: leading the struggle against apartheid; the Rivonia Trial and the "I Am Prepared to Die" speech; 27 years in prison; negotiating the end of apartheid with F. W. de Klerk; becoming South Africa's first black head of state; the Truth and Reconciliation Commission; the Nobel Peace Prize

t: Mandela joined the African National Congress in 1943, moved from non-violent protest to co-founding the armed group Umkhonto we Sizwe in 1961, and was sentenced to life imprisonment in 1964.
Released in 1990 after 27 years, he negotiated an end to apartheid with President F. W. de Klerk and led the ANC to victory in the multiracial election of 1994.
As president he made reconciliation between the country's racial groups his primary task, while critics on the left and right, and later he himself, faulted parts of his record.
dyk: While a student at the University of Fort Hare, Mandela performed in a drama society play about Abraham Lincoln. He left the university without a degree after being suspended for joining a boycott over the quality of the food.
ev: Mandela helps to found the African National Congress Youth League and sits on its executive committee
He opens the Defiance Campaign at a Durban rally, is arrested, and is elected president of the ANC's Transvaal branch
Acquitted in the Treason Trial, he co-founds Umkhonto we Sizwe, which announces itself with 57 bombings in December
At the Rivonia Trial he is found guilty of sabotage and conspiracy and sentenced to life imprisonment
President F. W. de Klerk announces his unconditional release, and he leaves Victor Verster Prison on 11 February
The ANC wins 63% of the vote in the first multiracial general election, and he is inaugurated as President of South Africa
He retires after one term and is succeeded by his deputy, Thabo Mbeki
Mandela dies at his home in Houghton at the age of 95

sections.early:
Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela was born on 18 July 1918 in the village of Mvezo in Umtata, then part of South Africa's Cape Province. His forename Rolihlahla is a Xhosa term colloquially meaning "troublemaker"; in later years he was known by his clan name, Madiba. His great-grandfather Ngubengcuka had ruled the Thembu Kingdom, but Mandela's branch of the royal family was ineligible for the throne and served as hereditary royal councillors. His father, Gadla Henry Mphakanyiswa Mandela, was a local chief and councillor to the monarch, sacked for corruption in 1926; his mother, Nosekeni Fanny, was Gadla's third wife.

He grew up in his mother's kraal at Qunu. Both parents were illiterate, but his mother, a devout Christian, sent him at about seven to a Methodist school, where a teacher gave him the name Nelson. When he was about nine his father died, and he was entrusted to the Thembu regent, Chief Jongintaba Dalindyebo, at Mqhekezweni. He went on to Clarkebury Methodist High School, to Healdtown and in 1939 to the University of Fort Hare, where he befriended Oliver Tambo. Suspended over a student boycott, he never returned.

In 1941 he fled an arranged marriage to Johannesburg, where the ANC activist Walter Sisulu found him work as an articled clerk in a law firm. He passed his BA exams in early 1943 and began studying law at the University of the Witwatersrand, where he was the only black African student. He joined the ANC in 1943, and in 1944 the ANC Youth League was founded with Mandela on its executive committee. That October he married Evelyn Mase, a trainee nurse.
sections.rise:
After the whites-only election of 1948 brought to power the party that became the National Party, which codified and expanded racial segregation as apartheid, Mandela and his allies pressed the ANC towards boycotts and strikes. He joined its national executive in March 1950 and was elected national president of the Youth League that year. At first opposed to a multi-racial front, he came to embrace one. On 22 June 1952 he addressed 10,000 people in Durban to open the Defiance Campaign and was arrested; the ANC's membership grew from 20,000 to 100,000, and in October he was elected president of its Transvaal branch. In 1953 he and Tambo opened the only African-run law firm in the country.

Repeatedly banned from public appearances, he concluded after the forced removals from Sophiatown in 1955 that violent action would prove necessary. He was arrested for high treason in December 1956; the judges returned a verdict of not guilty on 29 March 1961. After police killed 69 protesters at Sharpeville in 1960 the government banned the ANC. In 1961 Mandela, Sisulu and Joe Slovo co-founded Umkhonto we Sizwe (MK), which planned sabotage at night, when civilians were not present, and announced itself with 57 bombings on 16 December 1961.

Captured on 5 August 1962, he was sentenced to five years for inciting strikes and leaving the country without permission. After a police raid on Liliesleaf Farm he was tried again at Rivonia, where he gave his three-hour "I Am Prepared to Die" speech, and on 12 June 1964 he was condemned to life imprisonment.
sections.deeds:
Mandela served 27 years in prison: 18 on Robben Island, where he broke rocks and worked in a lime quarry whose glare permanently damaged his eyesight, then from 1982 in Pollsmoor Prison and from December 1988 in Victor Verster Prison. In February 1985 he spurned President P. W. Botha's offer of release if he rejected violence. From 1987 he held secret meetings with the Minister of Justice, Kobie Coetsee. President F. W. de Klerk legalised the banned parties in February 1990, and Mandela walked free on 11 February.

Elected ANC President in July 1991, he led the party through negotiations broken by violence between ANC and Inkatha supporters that cost thousands of lives. He and de Klerk agreed on an interim constitution and a multiracial election, and were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. On 27 April 1994 the ANC took 63% of the vote, and Mandela was inaugurated on 10 May at the head of a Government of National Unity that included the National Party and Inkatha.

He saw national reconciliation as the primary task of his presidency. He oversaw the formation of a Truth and Reconciliation Commission, chaired by Desmond Tutu, which granted individual amnesties in exchange for testimony, and he presented the 1995 Rugby World Cup trophy wearing a Springbok shirt. A new constitution was agreed in May 1996. His government introduced parity in grants across racial groups and free healthcare for children under six and pregnant women; by the 1999 election the ANC could claim 750,000 houses built, 2 million people connected to electricity and water access extended to 3 million.
sections.opponents:
Mandela was a controversial figure for much of his life. The apartheid state banned, tried and imprisoned him, and President Botha considered him a dangerous "arch-Marxist". During the 1980s political figures in the Western world labelled him a terrorist for his embrace of political violence; Ronald Reagan and Margaret Thatcher both considered the ANC a terrorist organisation, and he remained on a United States terrorism watchlist until 2008. He denied being a communist, but research published in 2011 strongly suggested that he had joined the South African Communist Party, which the party and the ANC confirmed after his death.

On the left, some in the ANC accused him of selling out by negotiating with the apartheid government and by not implementing the Freedom Charter; MK activists criticised his ceasefire of 1990, and many in the ANC derided the economic policy of 1996 as neo-liberal. Militant black critics, among them his estranged wife Winnie, charged that the ANC was more interested in appeasing the white community than in helping the black majority.

His government was criticised for failing to deal with the HIV/AIDS pandemic, with 10% of the population HIV positive by 1999, a neglect he later admitted, and for failing to combat crime and corruption. Western governments criticised his friendships with Fidel Castro and Muammar Gaddafi. In his private life his first wife, Evelyn, claimed in 1956 that he had physically abused her, which he denied. The scholar Rita Barnard wrote that his chiefly bearing in some sense "went against the spirit of democracy".
sections.last:
Mandela had never planned to stand for a second term. He stepped down as ANC President in December 1997, hoping that Cyril Ramaphosa would succeed him, but the party elected Thabo Mbeki. On his 80th birthday in July 1998 he married the Mozambican political activist Graça Machel, widow of the former president Samora Machel. He gave his farewell speech to Parliament on 29 March 1999 and retired that June; 80% of South Africans polled in 1999 expressed satisfaction with his performance as president.

He found seclusion difficult and returned to a busy public life, working with the Nelson Mandela Foundation, founded in 1999 to focus on rural development, school construction and combating HIV/AIDS. He urged Mbeki's government to ensure access to anti-retrovirals and, in January 2005, made public that AIDS had caused the death of his son Makgatho. He opposed the 1999 NATO intervention in Kosovo and in 2003 spoke out against the planned war in Iraq. In June 2004, aged 85, he announced that he was "retiring from retirement". In 2007 he announced the formation of The Elders, and he made his final public appearance at the closing ceremony of the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

From February 2011 he was repeatedly hospitalised with respiratory and lung infections. He died on 5 December 2013, aged 95, at his home in Houghton, surrounded by his family. President Jacob Zuma proclaimed ten days of national mourning; the body lay in state at the Union Buildings in Pretoria from 11 to 13 December, and a state funeral was held on 15 December in Qunu.
sections.legacy:
By the time of his death Mandela was widely considered within South Africa "the father of the nation" and "the founding father of democracy", and abroad a "global icon". He received more than 250 awards, among them the Nobel Peace Prize and the Soviet Union's Lenin Peace Prize. In November 2009 the United Nations General Assembly proclaimed his birthday, 18 July, as "Mandela Day", and in 2015 it named the amended Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners "the Mandela Rules".

His fame grew during his imprisonment in the 1980s, when he became the world's most famous political prisoner. The biographer Martin Meredith wrote that he gained "mythical status" as a symbol of resistance, and his official biographer Anthony Sampson that the myth became "so powerful that it blurs the realities", turning Mandela into "a secular saint". Mandela himself said: "I was not a messiah, but an ordinary man who had become a leader because of extraordinary circumstances." He is often cited beside Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr..

Within a decade of his presidency his era was widely thought of as "a golden age of hope and harmony". Assessments remain divided: the biographer Tom Lodge saw his politics as chiefly about "morally exemplary conduct" and only secondarily about ideological vision, while concerns were voiced that he placed his celebrity above the transformation of his country. The term "Mandela effect", for a false memory shared by many people, comes from the widespread false memory that he died in prison in the 1980s.

summary: Nelson Mandela joined the African National Congress in 1943, turned to sabotage in 1961 and spent 27 years in prison. Released in 1990, he negotiated the end of apartheid, won the 1994 election and, as South Africa's first black president, put reconciliation first. He died in 2013, honoured worldwide and criticised from both left and right.
